comparison: Both support herbivorous/folivorous interpretations for Bohaiornis (C4, C51-C54). OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of converging evidence from multiple proxies. Peer reviewers accept this as part of 'the most comprehensive analysis' with no challenges to herbivorous interpretations.

Both support herbivory in Parabohaiornis (C4, C55-C56). OpenEval notes less diagnostic clarity than Bohaiornis but multiple supporting lines of evidence. Peer reviewers accept herbivorous interpretations without specific concerns.

Perfect alignment on raptorial carnivory in Longusunguis (C5, C38, C63-C64). Both find converging evidence from pedal morphometrics and dental morphology well-supported. Peer reviewers congratulate authors on detailed study with no concerns.

Both support frugivory/generalist interpretation for Zhouornis (C6, C60-C62). OpenEval notes evidence doesn't definitively distinguish between dietary modes. Peer reviewers accept as part of comprehensive analysis showing bohaiornithid diversity.

Both acknowledge dietary uncertainty for some taxa (C7). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to intermediate values and reconstructed material. Peer reviewers accept ambiguous assignments as reflecting generalist or varied diets.

Both support body mass analysis and statistical methods (C25-C28, C31). OpenEval emphasizes robust phylogenetic HSD and bootstrap confidence intervals. Peer reviewers describe dataset as 'solid' and foundational to dietary interpretations.

Perfect agreement on mechanical advantage measurements (C32-C34). Both note clear patterns distinguishing Bohaiornis despite limited predictive power for diet in extant birds. Peer reviewers accept MA as part of comprehensive multi-proxy approach.

Perfect agreement on FEA results (C35-C37). Both support findings that bohaiornithids have stronger jaws than other enantiornithine families. Peer reviewers accept FEA despite lack of phylogenetic signal in extant data.

Both support pedal morphometric analysis (C39-C40, C137-C140). OpenEval notes phylogenetic signal validates framework but uncertainty about Sulcavis. Peer reviewers accept revised analysis addressing toe arrangement concerns.

Both support skull morphometric patterns (C41-C45). OpenEval notes bohaiornithids don't conform to extant correlations, limiting interpretive power. Peer reviewers accept skull shape data as contributing to dietary interpretations.

Divergent evaluations of ancestral state reconstructions (C8, C46-C50, C75-C78). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to high uncertainty and only 47% direct evidence support. Peer reviewers find ancestral generalist proposal 'curious, thought-provoking' and SUPPORTED.

OpenEval rates ancestral reconstructions UNCERTAIN (C46-C50) noting heavy influence of taxon sampling. Peer reviewers SUPPORT the reconstructions, accepting uncertainty for some nodes as reflecting limited data.

Perfect agreement on progressive jaw strengthening and dietary diversification across families (C65-C71). Both support clear stepwise pattern in FEA data. Peer reviewers accept as key contribution showing ecological diversification.

Perfect agreement on comparative evolutionary argument (C9, C79-C83). Both support 25-million-year diversification timeframe and comparison to crown birds. Peer reviewers find proposal 'curious, thought-provoking' with implications for K-Pg extinction studies.

Divergent evaluations of durophagy hypothesis refinement (C16-C17, C119, C124). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on quantitative comparisons. Peer reviewer R17 rates UNCERTAIN due to fundamental concerns about comparing toothed vs. beaked birds.

OpenEval rates herbivory mechanism (C57-C59, C119-C120) as UNCERTAIN due to indirect evidence and speculation about hindgut specialization. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific mechanistic claim.

Perfect agreement on methodological limitations and sensitivity analyses (C96-C97, C117-C118). Both support reconstruction methodology as appropriate given fossil preservation. Peer reviewers note authors 'did most paleontologists could do.'

Both support pedal analysis refinements (C137-C140). OpenEval emphasizes robustness to anisodactyl taxa addition. Peer reviewers explicitly state ontogenetic concerns 'have been addressed in the revised manuscript.'

OpenEval supports revision of piscivory conclusion for specific taxon (C113) based on improved body mass data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific taxonomic revision.

Divergent evaluations of tooth morphology interpretations (C125-C126). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED that similar teeth across different diets indicates phylogenetic signal. Peer reviewer R17 rates UNCERTAIN due to concerns about comparing toothed vs. beaked birds.

Strong agreement on ontogenetic considerations (C99, C141-C145). Both support conclusion that specimens are adequately mature for comparison. Peer reviewer explicitly states 'This concern has been addressed in the revised manuscript.'

Perfect agreement on comparative dataset quality (C23-C24, C100-C103). Both emphasize substantial sample sizes provide robust frameworks. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'large amount of data forms a solid dataset.'
OpenEval supports taxonomic refinement for cf. Sulcavis specimen (C112) based on shared synapomorphies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific taxonomic assignment.

Peer reviewer R16 rates UNCERTAIN the fundamental assumption of comparing toothed enantiornithines to beaked neognaths (C116, C20-C22), stating assumption 'is not made explicit, let alone justified.' No corresponding OpenEval result addresses this methodological concern.

Peer reviewer R18 rates UNCERTAIN the comparability of kinetic vs. akinetic skulls (C104), noting 'we cannot necessarily make those same assumptions when comparing the kinetic skull of a neognath to the akinetic skull of an enantiornithine.' No corresponding OpenEval result addresses this concern.

Peer reviewers accept the knowledge gap and study motivation (C1-C2, C12-C14) as important, describing work as addressing 'surprisingly diverse diets' and acknowledging dietary ecology is 'challenging by all means.' No corresponding OpenEval result evaluates study motivation claims.
